headline: Recommended City Council fund consistent school zone signage through an upcoming CIP; no action on Sewalls Falls Road crossing request.
summary: Members reviewed July and August 2026 crash data and noted more crashes involving E-bikes. They recommended no City action at this time on a Sewalls Falls Road crossing request, and recommended Council fund consistent school zone signage through an upcoming CIP. No action was needed on a Weir Road corner concern.
decisions: Approved the July 21, 2026 draft meeting minutes as amended, by unanimous consent.
Recommended no City action at this time on the speed and pedestrian safety request for Sewalls Falls Road, citing the crossing guard; passed unanimously.
Recommended the City Council appropriate funding through an upcoming CIP, with the School District, for consistent school zone signage; passed unanimously.
No action necessary at this time on safety concerns at the sharp corner on Weir Road.
Agreed a short double yellow line around the N Main Street and Horseshoe Pond Lane island could help clarify traffic flow; Hill to provide a sketch.

decision_evidence.quote: On a motion made by Bass seconded by Demers, the meeting minutes of July 21, 2026 were approved as amended. The motion passed by unanimous consent.

Bass moved to recommend no action by the City at this time, noting that a crossing guard is provided at this intersection and is the safest means of facilitating pedestrian crossings during school operations.

Bass further moved to recommend that the City Council appropriate funding through an upcoming CIP, in collaboration with the School District, to implement consistent signage throughout the City’s school zones, similar to the recommendations outlined in the 2008 Concord School Zone Signage Worksheet, Hill seconded the motion, all in favor, and the motion passed unanimously.
The Committee agreed that, given the roadway geometry and low traffic volumes, no action is necessary at this time.

After noting that pavement markings had not been restored following the resurfacing project, the Committee agreed that adding a short double yellow line leading up to and around the island could help clarify traffic flow. Demers asked Hill to provide a sketch of the proposed pavement markings.

plain_text:
September 15, 2026 
Page 1 of 3 
 
CITY OF CONCORD 
TRAFFIC OPERATIONS COMMITTEE 
MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 15, 2026 
 
The Traffic Operations Committee (TOC) met at 9:00 am on September 15, 2026 
in the Second Floor Conference Room, 41 Green Street 
 
Attendees: Alec Bass, Michael Bezanson, Matthew Casey, Matt Cashman, Kevin Demers, 
Karen Hill, and Harold Palmer 
 
Absent: Fred Reagan  
 
Guests:  
1.   Introductions  
 
2.   Approval of Minutes  
 a.  July 21, 2026 TOC Draft Meeting Minutes 
On a motion made by Bass seconded by Demers, the meeting minutes of July 21, 
2026 were approved as amended. The motion passed by unanimous consent. 
 
3.   Review City-Wide Crash Data 
Crash data was provided to the Committee for review. 
 a.   July 2026 
There were 80 reportable crashes in July 2026. This compares with 83 reportable 
crashes in July 2025. 17 crashes resulted in injuries. There were no fatality involved 
crashes. There were 2 reported crashes involving pedestrians and 2 involving 
bicyclists.  
 
 b.  August 2026 
There were 77 reportable crashes in July 2026. This compares with 100 reportable 
crashes in August 2025. 17 crashes resulted in injuries. There were no fatality 
involved crashes. There were 0 reported crashes involving pedestrians and 3 
involving bicyclists. 
 
Casey summarized the data and mentioned, again, that we are seeing more 
crashes involving E-bikes. 
 
4.   Council/Committee Updates 
Hill noted that Council reviewed and discussed the report from the Transportation 
Policy Advisory Committee regarding the Middle School project. Bezanson shared 
that Council ultimately voted to accept the report. 
 
5.   Project Updates 
Hill noted that GSD is working with GMI to construct the Broadway at Wiggins 
Street intersection improvements and Green Street/Civic District sidewalk 
improvements.
September 15, 2026 
Page 2 of 3 
 
 
Demers noted that GSD has completed the resurfacing of the Woodcrest Heights 
neighborhood and still needs to apply final pavement markings. He added that 
Prescott/Thomas Streets are under construction.  
 
Bezanson added that final paving of Airport Road is set to begin this week or next. 
 
6.   Unfinished Business  
 a.  None 
 
7.   New Business 
 a.  Resident request in regards to speed and pedestrian safety concerns on Sewalls 
Falls Road with request for a WEEBLE at Sewalls Falls Road at Sylvester Street and 
speed feedback signs at Beaver Meadow School 
Hill provided a summary of the residents’ requests. She explained that WEEBLEs 
are removed in the fall to accommodate long-line striping and winter operations 
and are typically redeployed in late spring, which does not align well with the 
school calendar. She also noted that this particular crossing is staffed by a crossing 
guard during school pick-up and drop-off hours. 
 
The Committee acknowledged that the number of turning movements at this 
intersection makes it a difficult location for placement of a WEEBLE. 
 
The Committee discussed prior conversations regarding the installation of curbing 
along this segment. Members agreed that accommodating drainage would be 
difficult and that the improvements would likely develop into a larger-scale 
project. 
 
Cashman added that the School District has discussed alternatives for traffic flow 
on the Beaver Meadow site, but that further consideration would require a traffic 
study. 
 
Hill shared a 2008 Concord School Zone Signage Worksheet, in which the City’s 
previous traffic engineer inventoried signage within the City’s school zones and 
recommended a consistent preferred sign package, including speed feedback 
signs. Hill noted that it appears the recommendations were never programmed or 
funded. 
 
Demers stated that he would follow up regarding where Sylvester Street and 
Sewalls Falls Road fall within the paving program. 
 
Casey stated that, in the interim, the School District should consider temporary 
measures to help alleviate vehicle queuing on Sewalls Falls. The Committee 
discussed the possibility of queuing vehicles on Second Street, double-stacking 
vehicles at the secondary driveway, and directing vehicles to exit onto Sewalls Falls 
Road.
September 15, 2026 
Page 3 of 3 
 
Bass moved to recommend no action by the City at this time, noting that a crossing 
guard is provided at this intersection and is the safest means of facilitating 
pedestrian crossings during school operations. Bass further moved to recommend 
that the City Council appropriate funding through an upcoming CIP, in 
collaboration with the School District, to implement consistent signage throughout 
the City’s school zones, similar to the recommendations outlined in the 2008 
Concord School Zone Signage Worksheet, Hill seconded the motion, all in favor, 
and the motion passed unanimously. 
    
Bass and Bezanson left at 9:55am. 
 
 b.  Resident request through SeeClickFix in regards to safety along the sharp corner on 
Weir Road 
The Committee reviewed a map of the area. Hill confirmed that the City does not 
allow or install mirrors within the public right-of-way. The Committee also 
discussed that a pedestrian sign would not be appropriate at this location. The 
Committee agreed that, given the roadway geometry and low traffic volumes, no 
action is necessary at this time. 
 
 c.  Resident request through SeeClickFix in regards to the island at N Main Street and 
Horseshoe Pond Lane 
The Committee reviewed a map of the area and confirmed that proper signage is 
in place. After noting that pavement markings had not been restored following the 
resurfacing project, the Committee agreed that adding a short double yellow line 
leading up to and around the island could help clarify traffic flow. Demers asked 
Hill to provide a sketch of the proposed pavement markings. 
 
8.    Next Meeting 
October 20, 2026 
 
9.   Adjourn 
On a motion made by Casey, seconded by Palmer, the meeting adjourned at 10:10 
am. All in favor. 
    
Minutes prepared by Karen Hill and Alec Bass
